doc.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Women in jazz efforts, Billy Taylor's festival and Marian McPartland
summary: She avoids all-women projects but plays the Mary Lou Williams festival and did a women's seminar with Marian McPartland at IAJE.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Have you been able to get involved in any of the — there are some women in jazz efforts around the country, have you been involved in those?
Not too much. I prefer to play with musicians that I choose for musical reasons.

But I am playing on Billy Taylor’s Mary Lou Williams Jazz Festival at Kennedy Center in May. And they did ask me in this case to bring a female band. So I’m taking some wonderful female musicians. It’s such a good festival that I made the exception there because I think it’s promoting women in the right way, and I think it’s all about the serious women jazz artists. But I do try to stay away from that as much as I can. I do play with some female players, but they would be because I choose them, not necessarily because I want to put a whole band together of women.
Right. Because they’re good at what they do.
Marian McPartland I think has been involved in some of those things. Have you ever gotten to meet her?

Yes. We worked together, as a matter of fact we put on a women’s seminar for young women at the IAJE conference last year in Chicago. And it was the professional women doing a seminar and concert for the young women, the students, both high school and college that were there. So Marian and I played on that concert for them, and talked to them and did a little mini clinic. She was wonderful. She moved so slowly to the piano, I was worried that maybe she was not feeling well or feeling tired or whatever. When she sat down she just blew everyone away.
